methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Daylight Computer is a Series A consumer tech company founded by Anjan Katta that has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of comparable public or private peers in the available dataset, limiting triangulation to a single methodology.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $10M total capital raised, yielding an implied valuation of $20M. This approach treats the cumulative funding as a proxy baseline and applies a typical Series A-to-next-stage advancement multiple. Given the limited methodological inputs, this single-method result dominates the analysis.

The triangulated range spans $17M (low) to $23M (median: $20M, high: $23M). The narrow band reflects reliance on a single applicable method rather than robust cross-validation. Key uncertainties include the absence of sector-specific comps, which prevents revenue or unit-economics benchmarking, and limited visibility into burn rate, unit economics, or market traction relative to peers. A more definitive valuation would require either access to comparable Series A consumer tech transactions or additional performance metrics (revenue run-rate, user growth, CAC/LTV dynamics) to support alternative methodologies.
